html:
I’ve kept a diary since 1997. At first my parents made me do it; then, in middle school, my teachers did. After a few years of being forced, something changed: I started to enjoy it, though I never wrote every day. When the mood struck, I might write every couple of days; other times I forgot about it completely and went half a year between entries.

Most of the time my diary is like an old friend I want to confide in every so often. I still get a little excited before I sit down to write. In high school, lyrical prose was all the rage, and my diary was mostly strings of rousing but empty parallel sentences. At university it became a pure outpouring of my own feelings, more sincere and more true to life.
